Definition: from G4862 and G3918; to be at hand together, i.e. now present:--be here present with.
BiblicalUsage: Festus presents Paul to Agrippa and says, King Agrippa, and all men which are here present with us, ye see this man. The word simply means being there together with others, and here it frames a trial: Paul stands in the middle of a room full of powerful people, and he is not afraid.
TheologicalSignificance: What grips me is that being present with God's people in a hard place is itself a witness, and I hold that Christ stands with me whenever I must stand before men.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
